1. Core Clinical Tension: An isolated, 5-mm vascularized interpalpebral bulbar conjunctival nodule in an otherwise healthy middle-aged woman that was clinically mistaken for an ordinary pterygium. Ocular involvement is an exceptionally rare manifestation of this protozoan disease and easily misdiagnosed as benign elastotic degeneration or ocular surface neoplasia.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint is set at the initial ophthalmic examination and presentation of the conjunctival mass, before surgical excision, histopathologic evaluation, and subsequent lesion recurrence.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pterygium was the primary clinical suspicion due to interpalpebral bulbar location and fibrovascular appearance, but excluded by histopathology revealing dense granulomatous inflammation and rapid recurrence; conjunctival neoplasia (OSSN) or pyogenic granuloma was considered due to fleshy vascularity, but excluded by absence of cellular dysplasia. The diagnosis pivots on histopathologic demonstration of epithelioid and multinucleated giant cells loaded with intracellular amastigotes.
case_prompt:
A 54-year-old previously healthy woman presents to an ophthalmology clinic complaining of a several-month history of a symptomatic lesion in her right eye, associated with a persistent foreign body sensation and local ocular discomfort.

On ophthalmic examination, visual inspection reveals a discrete, erythematous, fibrovascular lesion measuring approximately 5 mm in length located on the nasal bulbar conjunctiva within the interpalpebral zone of the right eye. The remainder of the ocular and systemic physical examination is otherwise unremarkable.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The nasal interpalpebral conjunctival location and fibrovascular appearance initially suggested a common pterygium, but surgical excision revealed intense granulomatous inflammation rather than solar elastotic degeneration, followed by rapid postoperative recurrence.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Initially, it was diagnosed as a pterygium.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Ocular surface squamous neoplasia / Pyogenic granuloma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A vascularized, recurrent ocular surface lesion raised suspicion for conjunctival dysplasia or reactive vascular granuloma; however, histologic analysis demonstrated a specific protozoan granulomatous etiology without dysplasia.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: During follow-up over a few weeks, the lesion recurred at the surgical site.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Histopathologic examination of the excised conjunctival mass revealed prominent stromal granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid and multinucleated giant cells packed with intracellular protozoan parasites.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histopathology of excised tissue showed granulomatous inflammation consisting of aggregates of epithelioid and giant cells through the stroma; some epithelioid cells were loaded with numerous Leishmania parasites.

editor_comments: Case prompt strictly limited to clinical presentation prior to surgical excision and histology; zero pathogen spoilers; exact quotes utilized.
